headline: No calendar or seasonality strategy beats SPY after California (or federal) tax with good confidence. Calendar timing loses in CA almost without exception: of 262 pre-registered rules (2000-2026), the median CA score is -3.47 pp/yr and none clears bar items 1-3. Only one kind of config clears items 1-3 in CA: the tax-managed 'cyclical SPDRs Nov-Apr / SPY May-Oct' rule (score +0.64 pp/yr, full_excess +1.18, ex10_beat 0.84, ex15_beat 0.91, boot_p 0.025; its Oct 1 neighbour scores +0.85). After 2002 it freezes into a static cyclical-sector tilt (XLK about 27%), and it fails item 4 (the family's walk-forward is negative) and item 6 (it needs XLK; 0 of 24 random menus clear items 1-3). In tax-deferred accounts, sector seasonality is the one persistent calendar effect (+0.98 pp/yr on full, +2.69 over 1986-2026), but it also fails the family walk-forward and depends on the basket. Carry nothing from this family forward.
findings: CA, calendar timing: of 262 pre-registered ETF-era rules (G1-G18), only 6 have a positive CA score. Four are once-a-year barometers (+0.21 to +0.70 pp/yr, ex10_beat 0.53, boot_p 0.44-0.68); two are constant-leverage controls. The CA median is -3.47 pp/yr and no rule clears items 1-3. Over 1986-2026 (235 rules, VFINX benchmark) the median is -3.18, 3 rules are positive and the best is +0.27. Switching twice a year turns deferred gains into 48.1% short-term gains.

The only CA configs that clear items 1-3 on full: tax-managed cyclical season Nov-Apr (gain budget 1%/yr): score +0.64, full_excess +1.18, ex10_beat 0.84, ex15_beat 0.91, ex20_beat 1.00, boot_p 0.025. Its Oct1-May1 neighbour: +0.85, +1.44, 0.91, 0.94, boot_p 0.035. These are comparable to the incumbent preset (+0.66, +1.54, 0.70, 0.83, 0.025).

That CA pass is a static tilt in disguise. The holdings replay shows it switches fully only while holdings show losses (2000-02, 2008). From 2010 on it averages XLK 26.6%, XLI 23.4%, XLB 20.6%, XLY 17.1%, SPY 12.3%. A gain budget of 0 does as well (+0.53 on screen). Its edge is in 2000-10 (+1.90 pp), with -0.04 in 2010-20 and -0.55 in 2020-26; the 5-year window started fresh in 2021 lost 2.0 pp/yr.

Static controls in CA: buying XLY/XLI/XLB/XLK once and never trading scores +1.21 on full, with every 10/15/20-year window and all sub-periods positive (+1.43 / +0.95 / +0.65), but boot_p is 0.287. Without XLK it scores +0.46 with boot_p 0.35. The 1986-2026 Fidelity version of the static basket scores +2.44 with boot_p 0.048 on long CA. This is a sector bet, not seasonality; refer it to the sector and factor families.

Neighbourhood of the CA candidate (11 neighbours on screen CA): all positive (+0.16 to +0.77) with 10-year beat rates of 0.76-0.88 (0.59 at a 5% budget). boot_p is at or below 0.071 only for budgets of 1% or less and 4 of 6 boundary pairs. Budgets of 2-5% and the Nov1-Apr1 and Dec1-May1 boundaries have boot_p 0.14-0.28; gb=0.05 on full scores +0.13 with boot_p 0.268.

PROTOCOL 5.3 for the CA candidate (G22): the same tax-managed rule on 24 random 4-fund menus from BROAD_EQUITY_POOL_2003 is positive on 8/24 (median -0.11 pp, best +0.25), and 0/24 clear items 1-3. The cyclical basket (+0.54) beats all 24. The six random menus with positive full_excess and boot_p of 0.11 or less all hold a tech fund. With the star removed (no XLK), full CA scores +0.46, ex10_beat 0.66, boot_p 0.30 and fails.

NONE: the famous effects lose to SPY in 2000-2026: Halloween/Sell-in-May into T-bills, Harding MACD, turn-of-month, pre-holiday, Mondays, Santa, barometers, presidential cycle, OpEx, quarter-end, same-month rotation, learned months. At near-zero costs (0+1 bp), TOM (-6.97), pre-holiday (-8.37), Mondays (-1.59) and Halloween/T-bills (-1.69) still lose, because the problem is time out of the market.

NONE, sector seasonality (cyclicals Nov-Apr, SPY May-Oct) clears items 1-3. Full: +0.98, ex10_beat 1.00, ex15_beat 0.94, boot_p 0.071. No-XLK: +1.46, boot_p 0.035. Oct1-May1: +1.21, boot_p 0.048. 1986-2026 Fidelity version: +2.69, boot_p 0.008, pre-2000 ho5 +2.49 (beat 0.78). After tax it loses (CA -2.17, FED -1.69).

Is the sector effect seasonality or a basket effect? Over 24 random menus the winter-only rule beats SPY on just 7 (median -0.22), but it beats holding the same menu all year on 19 (median +1.35). Reverse-season placebos lose (-0.66 ETF, -0.86 long). Among all 126 four-SPDR baskets the cyclical one ranks 11th (58% positive, median +0.07). On Fidelity funds it ranks 1st of 126, but 120/125 other baskets also beat VFINX (median +1.10), and an equal-weight 9-sector all-year basket scores +1.74, so the long-history evidence mixes in fund selection.

Post-publication decay (long_screen, 5-year windows by start era): in NONE, Halloween/Harding/January barometer are positive only for 1986-87 and 2000-02 starts and lose 6-7 pp/yr for 2013-21 starts. Sector seasonality and the small-cap January switch stay positive in every era in NONE, but in CA sector seasonality is negative for every start era except 2000-02.

Family selection test (item 4): with yearly decisions the ETF-era walk-forward loses out of sample: family CA -2.97 pp/yr (beat 0.17), NONE -3.90; sector sub-family CA -0.57, NONE -1.22. Over 1986-2026 the family is about zero (CA -0.43, NONE -0.02) and the sector sub-family is positive (NONE +3.73, CA +1.86), but only from 1996-2008 decisions; 2009+ decisions range -1.7 to +1.8. The DSR of each set's best config is at most 0.27 (0.81 for the long NONE sector set). PBO is 0.03-0.48, except 0.65 for the full-history ETF NONE family.

Leverage is not seasonality. SSO in Nov-Apr / SPY in May-Oct scores +4.32 in NONE (boot_p 0.162, max DD -75%) versus a constant 1.5x SSO/SPY mix at +3.68 (boot_p 0.117, DD -73%). In CA the seasonal version scores -1.33 and the constant one +2.77 (boot_p 0.174).

Verified predecessor material: the scheduled NYSE calendar matches the SPY/VFINX/^GSPC data calendars from 1980 except for 12 unscheduled closures; the raw-effects table reproduces exactly; May-Oct SPY beat VFISX in 19 of 26 years (2000-2025). Corrections: barometer boot_p is 0.44-0.68, not 0.6-0.9; config counts are updated; the 'same-season ranking' signal was drafted but never added or run.

hindsight_checks:
PROTOCOL 5.3 checks were run for both candidate lines.

CA tax-managed cyclical season:
- The same tax-managed rule on the same 24 random 4-fund menus from BROAD_EQUITY_POOL_2003 (G22, screen CA) is positive on 8/24 (median -0.11 pp, best +0.25), and 0/24 clear items 1-3. The cyclical basket (+0.54 on screen) beats all 24, and the six random menus with positive full_excess and boot_p of 0.11 or less all hold a tech fund (XLK/IYW/IGV/QQQ/SOXX).
- Star removed (no XLK): full CA +0.46, ex10_beat 0.66, boot_p 0.30, which fails.
- Static controls: never-rebalanced cyclicals +1.21 (boot_p 0.287); without XLK +0.46 (boot_p 0.35).
- The config itself (G19) was built after the G12 sector result was seen.

NONE sector seasonality:
- Same rule on 24 random menus (G21, screen NONE): beats SPY on 7/24 (median -0.22), but beats the same menu held all year on 19/24 (median +1.35).
- All 126 four-SPDR baskets in Nov-Apr: the cyclical basket ranks 11/126; 73/125 others are positive (median +0.07); by sector, baskets with XLE/XLB/XLY/XLI help and XLF/XLP/XLU hurt.
- Long history (Fidelity Select): the cyclical basket ranks 1/126, but 120/125 others also beat VFINX (median +1.10), so fund selection is mixed in.
- Removing XLK improves NONE (+1.46).
- The pre-2000 holdout supports it (ho5 +2.49), but the published sector-Halloween study used data through the mid-2000s, so only the post-2009 years are truly out of sample: 2010-20 +0.77, 2020-26 -0.22 pp.
- Reverse-season placebos lose in both eras.

Other checks:
- The scheduled-calendar construction was verified against the data calendars (12 unscheduled closures only), so there is no calendar look-ahead.
- Learned and same-month rules use only prior years.

Leverage (SSO) is labelled separately.
concerns: Multiple testing: 493 ETF-era and 369 long-era configs. The deflated Sharpe of each set's best config is at most 0.27 (0.81 for the long NONE sector set), and walk-forward selection is negative in the ETF era.

The CA pass is a static cyclical-sector tilt in disguise. Its boot_p of 0.025 rests on one path, the 2000-01 start, which happened to sell XLK in May 2000 and harvest losses through 2000-02. Its edge is in 2000-10, it needs XLK, and the 2021 fresh-start window lost 2.0 pp/yr. It concentrates in growth/tech, the same regime risk as the incumbent preset.

The long-history sector proxies are narrow, actively managed Fidelity Select funds (Retailing, Defense & Aerospace, Materials, Technology). Their historical loads and redemption fees are not modelled, and their all-year buy-and-hold already beats VFINX by 2-3 pp/yr. FSDPX starts 1986-09, so in 1986 the CalSignal basket is 75% invested.

The safe=long Halloween variants (best G1/G8 in NONE) are partly a duration bet on the 1986-2020 bond rally. Bond interest is taxed as deferred gains in the engine (PROTOCOL 5.5), which flatters them in CA, and they still lose in CA.

The engine pays each January's tax from cash even when fully invested, so cash runs negative at 0% until the next sale (avg cash -1.3% for standard sector-season in CA). This flatters taxable switching rules slightly; the CA candidate is unaffected (avg cash +0.02%). CalSignal(cover_tax=True) exists but was not needed for the negative verdicts.
The screen protocol has only 12 fifteen-year windows, so ex15_beat is coarse there. Verdicts use full and long.
The ETF-era basket placebo ran in CA for only 44 of 125 baskets (from the predecessor's interrupted run); NONE is complete. The long-era basket placebo ran in NONE only.
untested_ideas: Learned same-season rotation (SameSeason signal drafted in research/lab/scratch/seasonal/sameseason_draft.py, never added to the module or run). It would learn the winter basket from prior years only, the proper out-of-sample test of sector seasonality without a textbook or hindsight basket.
Sector seasonality on broad sector index proxies before 1998 instead of narrow Fidelity Select industry funds, to separate fund selection from seasonality in the long history.
A random-menu and walk-forward check of the static never-rebalanced cyclical basket as a stand-alone CA strategy. It is a sector-tilt idea for the sector_deep/factor_style families.
cover_tax=True (stricter cash handling of the annual tax bill) applied to every taxable switching rule. It would only lower already-negative CA results.
Asset location: run the seasonal or leveraged rule in a tax-deferred account and buy-and-hold SPY in the taxable one. The engine models one account only.
Calendar overlays on new contributions or dividends instead of switching existing holdings. The engine has no cash flows.
lab_bugs: report.diagnostics -> metrics.monthly_matrix(recs).dropna() silently truncates the PBO/DSR sample of a whole config set to the latest-starting config's months. One UPRO config (first screen start 2010-01) cut the ETF-era seasonal family from 319 to 199 months. Suggest computing PBO on configs with full history, or reporting the sample length.

report.diagnostics calls metrics.walk_forward(step_quarters=4), which steps 4 entries of protocol.starts. That is yearly on full/long (quarterly starts) but every 4 years on screen/long_screen (yearly starts), so screen diagnostics have only 3 (10/5) or 4 (5/3) walk-forward decisions and oos_beat is from n=3. Suggest stepping by calendar time (e.g. one year) rather than list entries.

Engine realism (site behaviour, not a lab-vs-site mismatch): Backtest settles each prior year's tax from cash on the first trading day of the new year even when the portfolio is fully invested. Cash goes negative, an implicit 0% loan, until the next sale. This slightly flatters strategies that realize gains, e.g. avg cash -1.26% for the standard sector-season rule in CA.
Minor: sweep.run_one measures rec['elapsed'] from before acquiring the CPU slot, so 'elapsed' includes slot-wait time under contention.
